test_title: RRB Group D Previous Year Paper (Held on: 25 Aug 2022 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: An object is placed on the principal axis of a concave lens of focal length 20 cm, at a distance of 10 cm. The magnification produced by the lens is _______ and the image is _______.
solution:
The correct answer is __**less than 1, erect**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The focal length of the concave lens is **–20 cm** (negative for concave lens).
 
• The object is placed at a distance of **10 cm** (object distance u = –10 cm). Using the lens formula: **1/f = 1/v - 1/u**.
 
• Substituting values: **1/(-20) = 1/v - 1/(-10)**. Solving for v, we get the image distance **v = -6.67 cm** (negative, meaning the image is virtual and formed on the same side as the object).
 
• The magnification (m) is given by: **m = -v/u**. Substituting the values: **m = -(-6.67)/(-10) = 0.667**, which is less than 1.
 
• The image is virtual, erect, and diminished (as magnification is less than 1).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Concave Lens:**

 
 
• Also known as a diverging lens.
 
• Always forms a **virtual, erect, and diminished image** for any object placed in front of it.
 
• Has a negative focal length.
 
 
 
• **Lens Formula:**
 
 
• 1/f = 1/v - 1/u, where f is the focal length, v is the image distance, and u is the object distance.
 
• Sign convention: For concave lenses, focal length is negative, object distance is negative when the object is in front of the lens, and image distance is negative for virtual images.
 
 
 
• **Magnification:**
 
 
• m = -v/u. The magnification indicates the size and orientation of the image.
 
• For concave lenses, the magnification is always less than 1 (diminished) and positive for virtual, erect images.
 
 
 
• **Virtual Images:**
 
 
• Formed when the rays diverge after passing through the lens, but they appear to converge on the same side of the object.
 
• Always upright and smaller than the object for concave lenses.
